articles.title: Noivo faz Primeira Comunhão para casar e vídeo de médica viraliza | G1
articles.standfirst: Médica brincou com a mudança de planos do noivo, que decidiu fazer a Primeira Comunhão antes do casamento. Publicação também motivou relatos de experiências semelhantes.
articles.summary: Noivo faz Primeira Comunhão para casar após mudar de ideia sobre namoro sério, em vídeo da médica Carla Rambo que motivou relatos semelhantes na web.
articles.body:
A médica Carla Rambo divertiu internautas ao compartilhar um vídeo do noivo, Jurandir Vilela, participando de uma celebração religiosa. Na publicação, ela brincou com a mudança de planos dele desde o início do relacionamento: "Não queria namorar sério... agora está até fazendo a Primeira Comunhão pra casar comigo!".

Nas imagens, o noivo aparece dentro de uma igreja, acompanhado de outras pessoas durante a cerimônia. O vídeo foi publicado em colaboração com o perfil dele e chamou a atenção de seguidores, que reagiram à situação com comentários bem-humorados.

Na legenda, Carla explicou que, apesar do tom de brincadeira, a história é verdadeira. "Brincadeiras à parte, foi um momento muito especial! O vídeo é meme, mas a história é real! Kkkk Obrigada, meu amor, por topar tudo e por viver cada etapa dessa história comigo. Te amo!" , escreveu.

Médica Carla Rambo ao lado do noivo Jurandir Vilela, que participou da Primeira Comunhão antes do casamento — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram de Carla Rambo

Médica Carla Rambo mostra pedido de casamento e aliança de noivado ao lado do companheiro Jurandir Vilela — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram de Carla Rambo

A publicação recebeu comentários de internautas que se divertiram com a mudança de planos do noivo. Uma seguidora brincou: "Arrumar um e colocar na casa do Senhor! Anotado!".

Outra comentou: "O famoso quem quer faz!" . Já uma terceira compartilhou uma experiência semelhante: "O meu também vai fazer a Primeira Eucaristia na sexta-feira para casarmos" .

Além das brincadeiras, seguidores parabenizaram o casal e deixaram mensagens de carinho. "Quando querem, fazem tudo... é só querer" , escreveu uma internauta. Outra comentou: "Que Deus continue iluminando o caminho de vocês dois" .

articles.title: Mulher é encontrada morta com sinais de violência em hotel de Jundiaí | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima de 35 anos deu entrada no imóvel acompanhada de um homem, que não foi localizado; Polícia Civil analisa imagens de câmeras de segurança para identificar o suspeito.
articles.summary: Polícia Civil investiga morte de mulher de 35 anos encontrada com sinais de violência em hotel no centro de Jundiaí; suspeito teria fugido pela janela do quarto.
articles.body:
Mulher é encontrada morta dentro de quarto de hotel em Jundiaí — Foto: Régis Rosa / TV TEM

Uma mulher de 35 anos foi encontrada morta em um quarto de hotel na Rua do Rosário, no Centro de Jundiaí (SP), nesta sexta-feira (23). A vítima apresentava sinais de violência pelo corpo.

Conforme apurado pela TV TEM , a mulher deu entrada no local acompanhada de um homem. A equipe do hotel acionou a Guarda Municipal depois que o período da hospedagem terminou e ninguém saiu do quarto.

Os agentes encontraram a porta fechada e, após conseguirem entrar, localizaram a vítima com sinais de violência. O Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi acionado e constatou a morte no local.

O homem que estava com a vítima não foi encontrado. Uma das suspeitas é a de que ele tenha fugido pela janela do quarto.

A polícia e a perícia estiveram no hotel e os investigadores procuram imagens de câmeras de segurança que possam ajudar a esclarecer o caso e localizar o suspeito.

articles.title: MPT denuncia assédio eleitoral na Câmara de Feira de Santana | G1
articles.standfirst: Ação foi protocolada nesta sexta-feira (23) após denúncia de coação. MPT pede medidas para garantir liberdade de voto e indenização de R$ 200 mil.
articles.summary: Ação foi protocolada nesta sexta-feira (23) após denúncia de coação. MPT pede medidas para garantir liberdade de voto e indenização de R$ 200 mil.
articles.body:
Câmara Municipal de Feira de Santana — Foto: Câmara Municipal

O Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) acionou a Justiça nesta sexta-feira (23) contra a Prefeitura de Feira de Santana e o presidente da Câmara Municipal, o vereador Marcos Lima (União Brasil), por suspeita de assédio eleitoral. O vereador nega a acusação. (Saiba mais ao final do texto)

O órgão pede medidas urgentes para impedir que trabalhadores sejam pressionados por conta do voto.

A ação foi motivada por denúncias de coação envolvendo áudios atribuídos ao presidente da Câmara. O MPT pede que a Justiça determine a suspensão de possíveis ameaças e a divulgação de uma mensagem pública reafirmando que nenhum trabalhador pode ser punido por sua escolha política.

As medidas devem proteger servidores concursados e comissionados, terceirizados, estagiários e aprendizes. O órgão também pede o pagamento de R$ 200 mil por danos morais coletivos e a aplicação de multas em caso de descumprimento das determinações judiciais.

A prefeitura foi incluída na ação porque a Câmara Municipal não tem personalidade jurídica própria.

O processo foi encaminhado à Vara de Plantão da Justiça do Trabalho, que vai analisar os pedidos urgentes. Até a última atualização, não havia informação sobre a decisão judicial.

O vereador disse que o suposto áudio não procede e chamou o caso de "fake news". Ele deve se pronunciar por meio de uma nota.

O g1 também procurou a Câmara Municipal da cidade, mas não obteve retorno até a publicação desta reportagem.

articles.title: Engenheiro tenta recorde e derruba 65 kg de chope na Oktoberfest em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Ação foi acompanhada por representantes do Guinness World Records, organização responsável por certificar os recordes mundiais. Ele carregou 27 canecas, mas não chegou até o final do percurso.
articles.summary: Ação foi acompanhada por representantes do Guinness World Records, organização responsável por certificar os recordes mundiais. Ele carregou 27 canecas, mas não chegou até o final do percurso.
articles.body:
O engenheiro civil Alex Bewiahn , de 34 anos, tentou quebrar o recorde mundial de carregamento de canecas de chope, nesta sexta-feira (23), mas deixou cerca de 65 kg de cerveja caírem no chão. A tentativa ocorreu na Oktoberfest Blumenau .

🍻 Ele precisava transportar 26 canecas por um percurso de 40 metros para superar a marca , mas não conseguiu completar a prova e desistiu após duas tentativas. O desafio é inspirado em um dos rituais mais emblemáticos da festa em Munique, na Alemanha.

Natural de Blumenau , no Vale do Itajaí, Alex carregou 27 canecas, cada uma com um litro de cerveja sem espuma, totalizando cerca de 65 quilos .

Na primeira tentativa, ele percorreu aproximadamente 20 metros antes de derrubar os recipientes. Na segunda, não chegou aos 16 metros. O engenheiro civil decidiu não fazer a terceira tentativa porque estava com as mãos muito inchadas.

Apesar da frustração com o resultado, Alex planeja disputar o desafio novamente em 2027. A ação foi acompanhada por representantes do Guinness World Records, organização responsável por certificar os recordes mundiais.

Alex foi convidado para a prova na quarta-feira (21), apenas dois dias antes do desafio. O convite surgiu após viralizar um vídeo em que ele participava do "desafio do lenhador" da Oktoberfest, competição tradicional de corte de toras de madeira.

Nesse intervalo, ele passou por um treinamento e chegou a concluir o desafio durante os treinos, segundo os responsáveis pela organização.

Desafio ocorreu na Oktoberfest Blumenau — Foto: Patrick Rodrigues/NSC

A prova ocorreu no Spaten Platz, setor localizado no Parque Vila Germânica. O objetivo era superar a marca de 26 canecas carregadas simultaneamente por 40 metros, recorde estabelecido em 2017, em São Paulo.

Para conquistar o recorde, o participante precisava completar o percurso sem segurar novamente as canecas durante a caminhada e sem derramar mais de 10% do líquido de cada recipiente.

As canecas também não poderiam ser apoiadas no peito, nos ombros ou em suportes presos ao corpo.

articles.title: Defesa Civil emite alerta de chuva forte e constante em Itapetininga | G1
articles.standfirst: Previsão é que Itapetininga (SP) registre 86 mm de chuva somente no domingo (25). Orientação é que moradores evitem áreas alagadas e se distanciem de rios e córregos.
articles.summary: A Defesa Civil de São Paulo emitiu nesta sexta-feira (23) um alerta para chuva na região de Itapetininga. O aviso vale até este domingo (25).
articles.body:
Orientação é que moradores evitem áreas alagadas — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Itapetininga

A Defesa Civil de São Paulo emitiu, nesta sexta-feira (23), um alerta para pancadas de chuva em cidades da região de Itapetininga (SP). O aviso prevalece até o domingo (25).

De acordo com o órgão, Itapetininga pode registrar 128 milímetros de chuva durante o período. A previsão é que a cidade tenha pancadas de chuva fortes e moderadas na sexta-feira, acompanhadas de raios e rajadas de vento.

Para o sábado (24), o alerta de pancadas de chuva, raios e rajadas de vento se mantém. O acumulado deve ser ligeiramente maior, com previsão de 22,1 mm.

A Defesa Civil aponta que, para o domingo, dia marcado para segundo turno das eleições presidenciais, o índice pluviométrico seja alto, com 86 milímetros. As pancadas de chuva são esperadas durante todo o dia.

Os temporais podem causar encharcamento do solo e elevação dos rios e córregos, aumentando o risco de alagamentos, enxurradas, transbordamentos e deslizamentos de terra. Há, também, a possibilidade de quedas de árvores e interrupções no fornecimento de energia elétrica.

Por isso, a orientação do órgão é que os moradores evitem áreas alagadas e não atravessem ruas inundadas. Confira a lista completa:

Não atravesse ruas inundadas ou trechos com correnteza;

Não procure abrigo sob árvores, postes ou estruturas metálicas durante tempestades;

Fique atento a rachaduras no solo, paredes, inclinações de árvores, postes e estalos em terrenos.

Em caso de emergência, a população pode acionar o Corpo de Bombeiros, pelo telefone 193, e a Defesa Civil, por meio do telefone 199.

articles.title: Grande BH tem temporal com granizo e rajadas de vento | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Esmeraldas, houve registro de queda de granizo e vendaval nesta sexta-feira (23); em Ribeirão das Neves, a chuva também provocou quedas de árvores.
articles.summary: Em Esmeraldas, houve registro de queda de granizo e vendaval nesta sexta-feira (23); em Ribeirão das Neves, a chuva também provocou quedas de árvores.
articles.body:
Um forte temporal foi registrado em cidades da Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte na tarde desta sexta-feira (23). Em Esmeraldas, houve queda de granizo e vendaval. Já em Ribeirão das Neves, a chuva também provocou quedas de árvores.

Na capital mineira, a Defesa Civil chegou a emitir um alerta de possibilidade de pancadas com raios e rajadas de vento em torno de 60 km/h. O aviso é válido até as 8h de sábado (24).

Veja, abaixo, os transtornos causados pela chuva na Grande BH :

Imagens enviadas por telespectadores da TV Globo mostram a grande quantidade de granizo que caiu em Esmeraldas durante o temporal desta tarde ( veja acima ).

Um morador gravou pedras de gelo espalhadas pelo bairro Itaporã. Ele disse que ficou muito assustado e não conseguiu sair de dentro do carro, porque a rua onde estava foi alagada. Também houve quedas de galhos de árvores na região.

Já no centro da cidade, uma telespectadora filmou uma enxurrada descendo pelo asfalto e o granizo caindo no jardim de casa. Segundo ela, a chuva durou cerca de 30 minutos.

Em Ribeirão das Neves, um morador do bairro San Genaro registrou o forte temporal com granizo ( veja acima ). De acordo com ele, a chuva durou aproximadamente 15 minutos e foi acompanhada por um vendaval.

O Corpo de Bombeiros disse que foi acionado para uma ocorrência de árvore caída na Rua Sete. Conforme a corporação, galhos puxaram a fiação durante a queda e obstruíram a via.

A prefeitura da cidade informou que a região do bairro Veneza foi mais afetada pela chuva, mas não houve chamado para a Defesa Civil.

Belo Horizonte registrou chuva em diferentes regiões. Nas quatro horas anteriores às 18h10, Venda Nova teve o maior acumulado, com 21,4 milímetros, seguida pelas regiões Nordeste (19,8 mm), Pampulha (13 mm) e Norte (11,6 mm), segundo a Defesa Civil.

A média climatológica para todo o mês de outubro na capital é de 110,1 mm.

articles.title: Orquestra Filarmônica de Santarém celebra 13 anos com rock e MPB | G1
articles.standfirst: Apresentação na Casa da Cultura reúne sucessos de Nirvana, Mamonas Assassinas, Chitãozinho & Xororó e Djavan com arranjos instrumentais.
articles.summary: A Orquestra Filarmônica de Santarém apresenta versões de Mamonas Assassinas e Djavan em concerto especial na Casa da Cultura neste sábado (24).
articles.body:
Orquestra Filarmônica de Santarém se apresenta neste sábado, na Casa da Cultura. — Foto: Divulgação: Agência Santarém

A Orquestra Filarmônica de Santarém (OFS) celebra 13 anos de história com um concerto especial neste sábado (24), às 20h, na Casa da Cultura de Santarém, no oeste do Pará. A apresentação terá versões instrumentais de músicas que marcaram gerações, misturando diferentes estilos em formato sinfônico.

O repertório do show inclui sucessos de artistas e bandas como Mamonas Assassinas, Chitãozinho & Xororó, Red Hot Chili Peppers, Nirvana, Engenheiros do Hawaii, Los Hermanos e Djavan. A proposta do grupo é aproximar o público da música orquestral por meio de canções populares e conhecidas, explorando novos arranjos e sonoridades.

Criada em outubro de 2013, a Orquestra Filarmônica de Santarém é considerada a primeira orquestra sinfônica do município. Desde a fundação, o projeto atua na promoção da música instrumental e no fortalecimento da formação cultural de novos músicos na região.

A trajetória da orquestra está ligada à Academia de Música da Filarmônica de Santarém, que é responsável pela formação dos integrantes. Atualmente, o grupo reúne cerca de 50 músicos sob a regência do maestro Rafael Brito, com apresentações que combinam instrumentos de cordas, sopros e percussão.

A estreia oficial do projeto ocorreu na Câmara Municipal de Santarém, durante uma sessão especial em comemoração aos 50 anos da Filarmônica Municipal Professor José Agostinho. Desde então, a orquestra segue ampliando suas atividades no cenário cultural do município.

articles.title: MPT apura envio de texto com teor eleitoral a funcionários do Zona Sul | G1
articles.standfirst: A carta não cita candidatos, mas diz que o Brasil vive um "esgotamento ético, moral e de modelo". O Ministério Público do Trabalho apura se houve assédio eleitoral aos trabalhadores. O Zona Sul não quis se pronunciar.
articles.summary: A carta não cita candidatos, mas diz que o Brasil vive um "esgotamento ético, moral e de modelo".
articles.body:
Supermercado Zona Sul no Jardim Botânicpo — Foto: Reprodução/Google StreetView

O Ministério Público do Trabalho no Rio de Janeiro (MPT-RJ) informou nesta sexta-feira que apura o envio de um texto com teor eleitoral pelos Supermercados Zona Sul a seus funcionários, às vésperas da eleição. No texto, um e-mail corporativo da empresa defende que "chegou a hora de mudar".

O caso foi antecipado pelo blog do colunista Ancelmo Gois, do Globo. Posteriormente, o g1 também teve acesso ao teor da carta. O MPT apura se houve assédio eleitoral aos funcionários.

O texto enviado para os funcionários por um e-mail corporativo é assinado por F.FLeta. O presidente da empresa é Fortunato Leta.

A carta não cita candidatos, porém, em um trecho, diz que"reconhecer o esgotamento de um ciclo não significa perder a esperança. Significa compreender que insistir nos mesmos erros não produzirá resultados diferentes".

Já perto do final, o autor escreve que "um país não se transforma verdadeiramente sem antes reconhecer que chegou a hora de mudar". No fim, pede que o funcionário "vote consciente".

O g1 procurou os Supermercados Zona Sul, mas a empresa não comentou. O MPT-RJ informou que tomou conhecimento do caso e registrou uma Notícia de Fato (NF) para apurar as informações.

"Temos a sensação de que o Brasil atravessa um momento particularmente difícil de sua história, marcado por uma crise que vai muito além das dificuldades econômicas e das disputas políticas. Vivemos um ESGOTAMENTO ÉTICO, quando os princípios, a coerência e o comportamento com o interesse público parecem ceder espaço a conveniências, interesses particulares e à ausência de responsabilidade. Um ESGOTAMENTO MORAL, quando a sociedade começa a se acostumar com situações que deveriam causar indignação, quando a confiança nas instituições e em suas lideranças se deteriora.

E, talvez o mais preocupante, um ESGOTAMENTO DO MODELO — político, econômico e institucional. Um modelo que parece ser incapaz de oferecer respostas consistentes aos desafios do País, promover crescimento sustentável, recuperar a confiança, valorizar o trabalho e construir perspectivas reais para as próximas gerações.

Não se trata apenas de construir governos, partidos ou ideologias. Trata-se de reconhecer que nenhuma nação consegue avançar de forma duradoura quando a ética perde espaço, a responsabilidade se dilui e os modelos de gestão deixam de responder às necessidades da sociedade.

O Brasil tem recursos, capacidade produtiva e talentos, que demonstram diariamente sua disposição para trabalhar e superar dificuldades. O que precisamos é transformar esse potencial em prosperidade, com instituições confiáveis, responsabilidade fiscal, segurança jurídica, justiça social e lideranças comprometidas com o interesse coletivo.

O País precisa de uma mudança de postura, de prioridades e de modelo. Reconhecer o esgotamento de um ciclo não significa perder a esperança. Significa compreender que insistir nos mesmos erros não produzirá resultados diferentes. Talvez o grande desafio do Brasil, neste momento, seja justamente este: recuperar valores, reconstruir a confiança e encontrar caminhos capazes de devolver à sociedade a perspectiva de um futuro melhor. Porque um país não se transforma verdadeiramente sem antes reconhecer que chegou a hora de mudar.

articles.title: Antiga Favela do Moinho, no Centro de SP, será transformada em parque; licitação será lançada na segunda | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto prevê investimento de R$ 41 milhões, com quadras esportivas, pista de skate, áreas de caminhada e espaços culturais; obras devem começar no início de 2027 e terminar em meados de 2028.
articles.summary: Projeto prevê investimento de R$ 41 milhões, com quadras esportivas, pista de skate, áreas de caminhada e espaços culturais; obras devem começar no início de 2027 e terminar em meados de 2028.
articles.body:
A área em que ficava a Favela do Moinho, no Centro de São Paulo , será transformada em parque. A licitação para as obras será lançada na próxima segunda-feira (26), com previsão de contrato de R$ 41 milhões e prazo de 24 meses. O projeto prevê quadras esportivas, pista de skate, espaços culturais e educativos, além de áreas para caminhadas e ciclistas.

O terreno, que hoje está completamente vazio, era ocupado por quase mil famílias. A comunidade enfrentou incêndios, operações policiais e protestos durante o processo de desocupação. A última família deixou o local em setembro, após as torres que marcavam a paisagem da favela serem demolidas.

A previsão do governo do estado é que as obras comecem no início de 2027 e sejam concluídas em meados de 2028. Depois da assinatura do contrato, a execução deve durar 18 meses.

O parque será instalado em uma área de pouco mais de 61 mil metros quadrados, que inclui o terreno da antiga favela e uma área próxima, sob o Viaduto Engenheiro Orlando Murgel e entre as linhas 7-Rubi e 8-Diamante de trens.

Antiga Favela do Moinho, no Centro de SP, será transformada em parque — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Histórico de incêndios e operações policiais

A ocupação do terreno começou depois que o antigo Moinho Central, que processava farinha de trigo, encerrou as atividades na década de 1980. Ao longo dos anos, os moradores conviveram com condições precárias e riscos, incluindo pelo menos quatro grandes incêndios. O maior deles ocorreu em 2011.

Em 2024, uma operação policial na Favela do Moinho prendeu Leonardo Monteiro Moja, conhecido como Léo do Moinho. Ele era apontado pelas investigações como chefe do tráfico na comunidade e integrante do PCC. Segundo a polícia e o Ministério Público, as drogas que saíam do local abasteciam a Cracolândia.

Em julho deste ano, o governo federal, proprietário da área, doou o terreno ao governo do estado, que acelerou o processo de retirada das famílias. Houve tentativas de resistência às desocupações, que foram acompanhadas por protestos.

Os antigos moradores foram encaminhados para imóveis de até R$ 250 mil. Do valor, R$ 180 mil foram custeados pelo governo federal, e o restante, pelo governo do estado.

A maioria das famílias optou por permanecer na região central. Segundo o governo, foram adquiridos apartamentos já existentes no mercado imobiliário, além de unidades prontas de diferentes projetos.

Parque terá quadras, pista de skate e espaços culturais

Imagens divulgadas pelo governo do estado mostram como deverá ficar o parque. O projeto prevê equipamentos esportivos e de lazer, áreas para caminhadas, espaços para ciclistas, pista de skate e ambientes destinados a atividades culturais e educativas.

Além do parque, o projeto prevê a implantação de uma nova estação de trem em um terreno vizinho, que pertence à Cea Gespe e a um proprietário particular e está em processo de transferência para o estado.

A licitação será lançada na segunda-feira (26). O contrato deverá ter valor de R$ 41 milhões e duração de 24 meses. Após a assinatura, a previsão é que as obras sejam executadas em 18 meses, com início no começo de 2027 e conclusão em meados de 2028.

articles.title: Joanna Darck: pesquisadora do PI é eleita Personalidade do Ano | G1
articles.standfirst: Piauiense participou da equipe do pesquisador Peter Ratcliffe, vencedor do Prêmio Nobel de Medicina de 2019, e receberá homenagem da Câmara Britânica em novembro.
articles.summary: A pesquisadora piauiense Joanna Darck, que integrou equipe do Nobel de Medicina, será homenageada pela Britcham como Personalidade do Ano após trajetória de superação.
articles.body:
A pesquisadora piauiense Joanna Darck Carola Correia Lima, 36, foi eleita Personalidade do Ano de 2026 pela Câmara Britânica de Comércio e Indústria no Brasil (Britcham), principal fórum da comunidade empresarial e governamental Brasil-Reino Unido.

Ela concorreu com outras três personalidades internacionais e receberá a homenagem em 26 de novembro, no Palácio Guanabara, no Rio de Janeiro.

Ao g1 , Joanna contou que recebeu a notícia com emoção e relembrou a trajetória construída ao longo dos estudos.

"Fiquei muito emocionada. De imediato pensei em todas as dificuldades da infância para estudar e viver com minha mãe", afirmou.

A pesquisadora também contou que enfrentou dificuldades financeiras ao longo da formação acadêmica e que chegou a vender pudins e roupas para ajudar a garantir renda para a família e dar continuidade aos estudos.

Joanna é formada em Ciências Biológicas pela Universidade Federal do Piauí (UFPI) — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

"Já moramos em fundo de igreja, já sofremos muito, já vendemos roupa, já vendemos pudim. Durante meus estudos, quando fiquei sem bolsa, trabalhei em restaurante em São Paulo", contou.

Formada em Ciências Biológicas pela Universidade Federal do Piauí (UFPI), Joanna, natural de Cacimba Velha, deixou o estado para dar continuidade à carreira acadêmica em São Paulo.

Durante o mestrado e o doutorado, foi contemplada com bolsas de estudo que lhe permitiram desenvolver pesquisas no exterior.

A pesquisadora passou três meses nos Estados Unidos e, posteriormente, conquistou uma nova bolsa para atuar na Universidade de Oxford, na Inglaterra, em 2018.

Após a experiência acadêmica no exterior, Joanna permaneceu no país por alguns anos e retornou ao Brasil em 2026.

Atualmente, ela atua como jovem pesquisadora e orientadora na Faculdade de Medicina da Universidade de São Paulo (USP).

Participação em pesquisa vencedora do Nobel

Esta não é a primeira conquista de destaque da pesquisadora piauiense. Em 2019, Joanna integrou a equipe ligada ao pesquisador Peter Ratcliffe, um dos ganhadores do Prêmio Nobel de Medicina.

A pesquisa premiada buscou compreender como as células detectam e se adaptam à disponibilidade de oxigênio no organismo, descoberta considerada fundamental para avanços no tratamento de diversas doenças.

Na época, em entrevista ao g1, Joanna afirmou que participar da equipe de um dos vencedores do Nobel representava um reconhecimento importante da trajetória construída desde o período em que iniciou os estudos sobre o tema ainda no Brasil.

Joanna afirma que busca inspirar outros jovens a acreditarem na educação como ferramenta de transformação social. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

"É uma honra, só tenho a agradecer", declarou.

Hoje, Joanna afirma que busca inspirar outros jovens a acreditarem na educação como ferramenta de transformação social.

"A educação é a única forma que temos de reduzir as desigualdades sociais no mundo. A meritocracia só existe quando partimos de pontos semelhantes. Por isso, essa conquista vale tanto, porque sabemos dos esforços necessários para chegar até aqui", afirmou.

A pesquisadora destacou que muitos estudantes brasileiros enfrentam desafios diferentes dos encontrados por alunos de instituições mais estruturadas, mas ressaltou a importância de ampliar as oportunidades de acesso ao ensino e à pesquisa.

"Tenho muito orgulho de hoje participar da formação da próxima geração de cientistas e de atuar aproximando a ciência da sociedade", concluiu.

Pesquisadora piauiense Joanna Darck Carola Correia — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

articles.title: Ditadura na Argentina: restos de 8 desaparecidos são identificados | G1
articles.standfirst: Estima-se que entre 2.200 e 2.500 pessoas tenham sido torturadas e assassinadas no local durante a ditadura civil-militar (1976-1983), que deixou cerca de 30 mil desaparecidos, segundo organizações de direitos humanos.
articles.summary: Ditadura na Argentina: restos mortais de oito desaparecidos foram identificados em uma vala comum em Córdoba, em local usado como centro de extermínio.
articles.body:
Familiares seguram cartazes com a imagem de Pascual Delfin Ludena, uma das oito vítimas identificadas a partir de restos mortais encontrados em uma vala comum — Foto: CESAR HEREDIA/AFP

A Justiça da província argentina de Córdoba anunciou nesta sexta-feira (23) a identificação de oito desaparecidos da ditadura, cujos restos mortais foram recuperados de uma vala comum, elevando para 38 o número de vítimas identificadas no local desde setembro de 2025.

Trata-se do local conhecido como Loma del Torito, um terreno do Exército argentino anexo à área onde funcionou, até 1978, o centro clandestino de detenção e extermínio de La Perla.

Estima-se que entre 2.200 e 2.500 pessoas tenham sido torturadas e assassinadas no local durante a ditadura civil-militar (1976-1983), que deixou cerca de 30 mil desaparecidos, segundo organizações de direitos humanos.

O trabalho da Equipe Argentina de Antropologia Forense (EAAF) permitiu recuperar centenas de fragmentos ósseos de um número indeterminado de vítimas.

O juiz Hugo Vaca Narvaja divulgou a identidade de quatro mulheres e quatro homens durante uma entrevista coletiva emocionante, ao lado de familiares das vítimas, que relataram suas histórias e as circunstâncias dos sequestros ocorridos em 1976.

A Justiça considera que os militares transferiram os restos mortais de outros locais em 1979 para ocultar provas antes de uma inspeção realizada naquele ano pela Comissão Interamericana de Direitos Humanos, motivada por denúncias da comunidade internacional.

Os identificados são Néstor Acosta, Pascual Ludueña, Claudio Nardini, Cecilia Pessina de Ávila, Mónica Protti de Guillén, Mercedes del Valle Ramírez, María Luisa Salto e Juan Carlos Soulier.

"Isso mudou tudo, já não preciso provar que ela desapareceu, o osso fala", disse Graciela Pessina, irmã de Cecilia, psicóloga sequestrada aos 28 anos, em 13 de agosto de 1976.

A identificação foi possível graças a um osso de sua mão, "com a qual Cecilia escreveu contos na adolescência, desenvolveu trabalhos estudantis, tocou Mozart", afirmou diante de uma sala lotada, onde estavam expostas fotografias de desaparecidos.

Rosa Ludueña, sobrinha de Pascual, um representante sindical da Fiat desaparecido aos 29 anos após se apresentar em uma delegacia depois de uma operação de busca em sua casa, destacou que seu tio foi identificado por meio de um osso do pé, com o qual "deixou uma marca que espero que se estenda a todos os que ainda não compreendem a dimensão do que aconteceu".

Sebastián Soulier, sequestrado junto com os pais quando tinha cinco meses e posteriormente entregue aos avós, soube que seu pai, Juan Carlos, está entre os identificados.

"Estou muito emocionado. Há 50 anos estamos procurando, é uma conquista coletiva. Na minha família ainda há dois desaparecidos, meu tio Luis e minha mãe", disse.

A EAAF anunciou que os trabalhos de identificação continuarão "até a conclusão da tarefa".

articles.title: The most popular baby names of 2026 are in. Here's why so many start with E.
articles.summary: Could Eliana dethrone Olivia? The E-name takeover is upon us.
articles.body:
The most popular baby names of 2026 have been revealed — and Olivia and Noah are still the favorites, according to BabyCenter data. But while the top names are holding steady, there's been a shake-up elsewhere in the top 10.

The Social Security Administration's (SSA) official list of this year's top baby names won't be available until May 2027, but BabyCenter's ranking of the most popular names of the year offers an early look at the choices parents are gravitating toward, along with some emerging trends.

Unlike the annual SSA rankings , which are based on applications for Social Security cards, BabyCenter's data comes from names that parents submit in real time through its app. That makes it less of an official ranking and more of a live snapshot of the names gaining traction right now.

In the girls' list, Eliana has jumped to the second spot, and Evelyn has risen five places to No. 9, joining the top 10. On the boys' list, Elias has entered the top 10 for the first time, and Leo has rejoined the list at No. 10, after falling out last year.

See BabyCenter's top 10 for girls and below, compared to 2025.

Of all 26 letters in the alphabet, E is the current favorite for girls. The vowel makes up 15% — the highest share — of BabyCenter's top 100 names. Three E names feature in the top 10 list alone: Eliana, Emma and Evelyn.

The name Eliana, in particular, is one to watch. It has climbed from No. 14 to No. 2 in two years — a rise that Steph Coffield, name adviser for BabyCenter, calls "meteoric." She adds, "If it continues with this momentum, we predict that it may become the top name next year."

Knocking Olivia off the top spot would be quite the achievement. It has been No. 1 on BabyCenter's list for six years. The SSA numbers tell a similar story: Olivia has topped its list for seven years running. Noah has held the top spot on BabyCenter's boys' list for four years in a row, whereas Liam has remained the SSA's No. 1 choice since 2017.

Just like the girls' list, names starting with the letter E are popular picks for boys too. J may lead the boys' top 100 with 14 options, but it doesn't have a single name in the top 10, while E has three: Elijah, Ezra and Elias.

Baby names beginning with E that featured in BabyCenter's top 100 lists

Coffield says that E names strike a great balance between modern and traditional. "They feel new and cool," she says, "but are still soft and melodious."

Right now, baby names are in their "soft era," according to Coffield, meaning that names with lots of vowels and soft consonants — like L, M and S — are very popular. "Eliana and Elias are perfect examples of how trendy these soft 'E' names are," she explains. "Both made big jumps in BabyCenter's top 10 this year."

E names come with plenty of options. Some of the most favored are long, such as Eleanor, Elizabeth and Emilia, but plenty are short, such as Emma, Ella and Eden. "It just goes to show how versatile 'E' is; whether you want a name that's short and sweet or long and elegant, there's an 'E' name out there for you," says Coffield.

The flip side of E's popularity is that the most-loved names are quickly becoming very common. If you want an E name that's more distinctive, here are some lesser-used options to consider.

Each of the suggestions below has been cross-checked against the SSA and BabyCenter's baby name records to ensure none currently appear in the top 1,000 list.

Emmylou: A combination of Emma ( meaning "whole") and Lou (meaning "warrior") that's the name of musician Emmylou Harris.

Edie: This Old English name is often a diminutive of Edith and means "prosperous in battle."

Elspeth: A Scottish name, Elspeth means "God is my oath."

Eudora: Of Greek origin, this vintage-sounding name means "good gift."

Erasmus: This Greek name means "beloved, desired."

Ender: Originating in Turkey, this baby name means "extremely rare."

Euan: Meaning "Yew," this Scottish name is strong and has close ties to nature.

Edmund: Closely linked to Edward, this Old English name means "fortunate protector."

articles.title: A Massachusetts buyer took a $3.85 million mortgage on a house sitting less than 14 feet from an eroding bluff; he demolished the property and went to court to challenge the loan
articles.summary: A Massachusetts coastal property became the centre of a legal dispute after its owner took out a $3.85 million mortgage on a house standing less than 14
articles.body: A Massachusetts coastal property became the centre of a legal dispute after its owner took out a $3.85 million mortgage on a house standing less than 14 feet from an eroding bluff above Cape Cod Bay. John Bonomi bought the Wellfleet property for $5.5 million in November 2021, but years of coastal erosion eventually forced him to demolish the house in early 2025. He has since taken JPMorgan Chase to court, arguing that the mortgage should be voided. The case raises questions about property valuations, lending decisions and the risks of buying homes along vulnerable coastlines.Why is the $3.85 million mortgage on the eroding Massachusetts house being challengedAccording to Realtor, Bonomi purchased the property at 1440 Chequessett Neck Road in Wellfleet, Massachusetts, after the house had already been identified as being at risk from coastal erosion. The foundation stood less than 14 feet from the edge of a bluff that had reportedly been retreating each year at the time of the sale.Despite the danger, Bonomi secured a $3.85 million mortgage from JPMorgan Chase to finance the purchase. The property, commonly known as the Blasch house after its original owners, had been built in 2010 by Mark and Barbara Blasch.The lawsuit, detailed by Lawsuit Bailbonds in its report on the case, identifies Bonomi as a retired New York attorney. He alleges that he lacked the mental capacity to enter into the mortgage agreement and that the bank took unfair advantage of his condition.JPMorgan Chase has denied the allegations. The bank maintains that it acted in good faith and followed reasonable commercial standards when providing the loan. The allegations have not been proven in court, and the dispute remains unresolved.The property's history reveals a long-running erosion problemThe threat to the house did not emerge suddenly after Bonomi bought it. Realtor reported that the original owners had been warned about the likelihood of severe erosion when they sought permission to build the property in 2010.From 2013 onwards, the Blasches placed large quantities of sacrificial sand beneath the property in an effort to slow the retreat of the bluff. They later sought permission to construct a 241-foot stone barrier, known as a revetment, to protect the land from further erosion.However, the town rejected the proposal, and the owners continued challenging the decision while the property was being prepared for sale in 2021.After purchasing the home, Bonomi continued the separate legal effort over the proposed coastal protection structure, according to Lawsuit Bailbonds. A Massachusetts court upheld the town’s decision in October 2023, and the complaint says a further appeal in 2025 left no practical way to challenge the rejection.The erosion continued despite efforts to protect the property. Realtor cited information from the Massachusetts Office of Coastal Zone Management indicating a long-term erosion rate of approximately 2.5-3 feet per year near the site. But periods of increased erosion, especially in the early and mid-2010s, meant the threat could change faster than long-term averages indicated.The owner says the mortgage agreement should not standLawsuit Bailbonds reported that Bonomi filed his case against JPMorgan Chase in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York in October 2025. The case, Bonomi v. JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., seeks to have the mortgage and the accompanying loan agreement declared voidable.The complaint presents 3 main claims. First, Bonomi was incapable of entering into the agreement because he was suffering from a prolonged manic episode related to bipolar disorder. He alleges that the bank knew, or deliberately avoided recognising, that he was not competent to sign the documents.The second ground is that the mortgage was unconscionable, i.e. the circumstances surrounding the agreement were so unfair that it ought not to be enforced. Bonomi alleges that the bank took advantage of his impaired mental state when approving the loan.The third claim seeks financial compensation for the losses he says followed from the agreement.According to Lawsuit Bailbonds, Bonomi paid approximately $21,053 a month towards the mortgage from November 2021 until September 2024, when he stopped making mortgage and property tax payments. The loan carried a fixed interest rate of 2.99% and was scheduled to mature in December 2051.His complaint seeks the return of approximately $695,000 in mortgage payments, alongside more than $750,000 in expenses associated with trying to preserve the property and eventually demolishing it.Owner left with land, disputed loan after demolitionBy the beginning of 2025, the danger of the house falling into Cape Cod Bay had grown so great that it needed to be torn down. Realtor reported that the house was removed before it could collapse into the water, while Lawsuit Bailbonds placed the demolition in February 2025.The complaint estimates that demolition cost approximately $250,000. The figures represent the owner's claims rather than amounts awarded by a court.The financial position of the property also changed considerably. According to Lawsuit Bailbonds, the town of Wellfleet assessed the property at more than $4.38 million in 2021. By January 2025, the land was assessed at $385,000, reflecting the dramatic change in its circumstances after the house was lost. Bonomi still owns the land, according to the report.The case highlights questions about coastal property lendingThe dispute also draws attention to the difficulties involved in assessing homes exposed to coastal hazards. Realtor explained that waterfront properties can retain considerable market value because buyers are willing to pay for ocean views, access to the water and desirable locations, even when erosion presents a serious risk.Often property valuations are based on comparable sales in the locality. If other vulnerable coastal homes continue selling for high prices, those transactions can support substantial valuations despite the underlying environmental danger.Standard mortgage appraisal guidelines don't always require appraisers to predict how long a property will last.They typically document the condition of the property and form an opinion about its value and marketability, and it is up to the lender to determine if further inspections are needed.Flood assessments may not fully capture the problem either. The Federal Emergency Management Agency does not include long-term bluff erosion in its standard coastal flood analysis. A property's flood designation therefore does not necessarily indicate how quickly the land beneath it is disappearing.As of September 2026, Lawsuit Bailbonds reported that JPMorgan Chase had filed its response, denying the allegations, and that the case remained in the pretrial stage without a ruling on the merits or a reported settlement.You use AI every day. articles.title: Hero who stopped Bend school shooter haunted by encounter: ‘I didn’t save everybody’
articles.summary: Kaylub Giamanco speaks for the first time about the day he brought down a school shooter in Bend, Oregon.
articles.body: A string of innocuous choices made by an Oregon father brought him to the elementary school where he killed a mass shooter in an act he believed would be his last. Police have credited the quick thinking and decisive action of Bend carpenter Kaylub Giamanco for confronting 16-year-old Griffin J. John II and stopping the teen shooter’s carnage on Oct. 15. The gunman had already killed a teacher and three young children at Silver Rail Elementary School and could have continued his attack had Giamanco, 36, not randomly ended up at the crime scene. In an emotional and harrowing interview with Oregon Public Broadcasting published on Friday, Giamanco recalled that fateful day. “I’ve always wanted to change the world, but I’ve felt small. I’m just a carpenter from Bend, Oregon. I was a nobody other than to my friends and family,” he told OPB. “I feel like if I’m going to have a voice, then I’ll be damned if I’m not going to use it to change this world, to make it a better place.” Giamanco’s presence in the neighborhood near Silver Rail came after a series of seemingly benign decisions the carpenter made that Thursday about lunch. Giamanco packed a midday snack but changed his mind about eating it, instead opting to drive home to have leftover tacos with his wife, he said. And on his way home, Giamanco had briefly considered going to a masonry shop to buy some bolts he needed, but again opted to go home for the tacos. Those choices led him to Brentwood Avenue near his children’s school just before 1 p.m., where he spotted a “man in black” with a long gun opening fire on a motorist and a woman mowing the school lawn, he recalled. Giamanco, who kept a .40 caliber handgun in his truck console, saw the killer toss his weapon over the school fence before climbing it himself. The father understood what was happening and “that’s when panic filled into my brain, and that’s when I opened my center console.” Giamanco, who has two girls, 5 and 10, attending Silver Rail, called 911 but couldn’t answer all of the dispatcher’s questions. “I said, ‘I’m sorry, I have to go in. People are going to die,’” said Giamanco. As Giamanco got closer to the school building, he kept a low profile and from his knees could hear the bloodshed. “That’s when I started hearing children pleading for their lives and then I started hearing gunfire and I just started army crawling faster and faster and I told myself, ‘This is probably the last thing that I’m ever going to do,’” he said. Giamanco crawled in through a shot-out window, reached the special education classroom and reracked his firearm in preparation for a deadly confrontation. He came upon the gunman and a teacher fighting for the killer’s gun. “I knew that he did not know that I was there,” Giamanco said. “And I fired.” The teacher fled, possibly believing Giamanco was a second attacker, he said. But the shooter was still alive and reaching for his gun. “He was scrambling for his weapon,” Giamanco said. “I looked at him and I shot him two more times to make sure that he couldn’t move because I was afraid of him shooting anybody else.” Police arrived shortly after and Giamanco pleaded with them to let him call his loved ones. “I called my wife to tell her that I’m not coming home for tacos,” he said. Then he called his mother. “She was just like, ‘OK, baby, calm down. You did the right thing. You’re a hero. You saved lives.’ And I was just like, “I didn’t save everybody. I didn’t get them all.’” Law enforcement officials have universally praised Giamanco for acting fast. Within hours of the shooting, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said of Giamanco and the teacher who fought with the killer: “I don’t think we can underestimate or under-appreciate that courage.” Giamanco said he’s been struggling to sleep since the mass shooting and can’t get that terrible day out of his head. “I relive, I see faces, I hear voices, I hear screams,” he said. The carpenter has not yet met the parents of the three children killed. Giamanco said he wants to tell them he’s sorry for not doing more. “I want to apologize for not saving their babies,” Giamanco said, his voice choking with emotion. “The gratitude for saving people’s children is awesome, but there were ones that I didn’t save.”

articles.title: Bodycam clip released in fatal police shooting of Mississippi one-year-old
articles.summary: The family lawyer says an allegation of shoplifting "does not warrant the death" of a child.
articles.body:
Mississippi authorities have released body camera footage showing how a toddler was fatally shot by a police officer responding to a report of shoplifting in a Walmart car park.

Kohen Wiley, aged one, was on his mother's lap in a moving car when officers surrounded the vehicle in the city of Senatobia on 14 June.

The state's attorney general found the policeman was justified in using force, and the officer's lawyer argued in a statement to the BBC that the driver was attempting to kill law enforcement.

The child's family disputes that the shooting was justified. Their lawyer, Ben Crump, has called the police response "excessive from the very start".

Crump said an allegation of shoplifting "does not warrant the death" of a child.

Kohen Wiley was riding in the vehicle with his mother, Vellesiya Wiley, and another woman at the time of the incident.

Senatobia Mayor Greg Graves confirmed to the BBC's US partner CBS that Hunter Foster, the officer who opened fire, had resigned.

The Senatobia Police Department did not immediately respond to the BBC's requests for confirmation.

The footage released by Mississippi authorities on Thursday shows a first-person perspective of the officer who opened fire.

After being told by a staff member that suspected shoplifters were getting away, five law enforcement officers run towards the car with guns drawn.

The vehicle reverses, crashing into a parked car, before pulling forwards.

The officer wearing the body camera raises his gun and aims it at the moving vehicle as he runs closer, shouting: "Stop!"

As the car closely passes the officer, he fires his gun, shattering the passenger-side window.

Four gunshots can be heard, as police command the driver to stop. The car continues to drive off slowly through the car park.

CCTV video from the storefront appears to show that at the moment the policeman opens fire, another officer is standing near the front of the moving vehicle.

"The driver of the vehicle was attempting to kill those 5 officers," Martin Zummach, an attorney representing the officer, said in a statement to the BBC, adding that his client "had no choice but to discharge his weapon".

"We are very sad for the loss of life," Zummach said. "But the outcome of the investigation was not only expected, but it was overdue."

The child's mother, Wiley, has denied she and her friend stole nappies from the store. No charges have been filed against them.

The boy's death has sparked protests and vigils in Mississippi.

At a news conference, relatives demanded accountability.

"After what I've seen today, I'm having a difficult time understanding the word, 'justified,' said LaSandra Williams, Kohen Wiley's grandmother.

articles.title: In 2019, Lucy Hale bought a 1940s Spanish-style home in Los Angeles for $2.95 million; after getting sober in 2022, she spent three years transforming it into a colourful retreat with a meditation room
articles.summary: A house can hold the story of a life in ways that photographs rarely capture.
articles.body: A house can hold the story of a life in ways that photographs rarely capture. For actor Lucy Hale, her Los Angeles home has witnessed heartbreak, personal change and the quiet work of finding herself again. What began as a sunlit Spanish-style retreat with understated, farmhouse-inspired interiors has since become a deeply personal expression of her evolving identity. Following her decision to get sober in 2022, Hale embarked on a three-year redesign that brought bold colours, vintage treasures, playful art and a dedicated meditation room into the 1940s property, turning it into a sanctuary that feels distinctly her own.A home with a historyHale purchased the Spanish-style residence in 2019 for $2.95 million, according to The Los Angeles Times. Tucked behind a gated, winding driveway in Studio City, the two-storey home occupies approximately an acre of land, with canyon views and a saltwater swimming pool offering a sense of seclusion from the city beyond.The 2,750-square-foot property features four bedrooms and 3.25 bathrooms, alongside walnut flooring, high ceilings and decorative tilework. French doors open from the chef’s kitchen and dining room onto a tiled patio with a brick fireplace, while the primary suite combines a clawfoot bathtub, artistic tiles and a cedar-lined walk-in closet.When Hale first moved in, she favoured a neutral, farmhouse-inspired aesthetic. The interiors were intended to provide a peaceful counterpoint to the demands of a career that had placed her in the spotlight from a young age. But, as her life changed, the house began to feel ready for a transformation of its own.Designing for a new chapterAs Architectural Digest reports, Hale’s decision to rethink her surroundings coincided with a period of significant personal growth. After getting sober in 2022, she began paying closer attention to her mental wellbeing and reconsidering what she wanted her home to represent.The actor eventually found her design collaborators in Ashley Drost and Marie Trohman of Los Angeles-based studio Proem. Drawn to their expressive, eclectic interiors, Hale wanted a home with greater depth, colour and personality.The designers developed an aesthetic they describe as moody femme, bringing together romantic flourishes, unexpected objects and a slightly irreverent sensibility. The renovation took three years to complete, allowing the residence to evolve into a collection of intimate spaces rather than a single, uniform design statement.Colour, character and collected treasuresThe new interiors move confidently beyond the neutral palette of the original renovation. Plum-coloured kitchen cabinets, pink accents, aubergine tones and richly textured furnishings introduce warmth and drama, while patterned fabrics and decorative wall coverings give each room its own identity.The primary bedroom takes cues from the intimacy of a Parisian jewel-box apartment, with textured linen wall coverings lending softness to the space. In the foyer, a life-size sheep sculpture creates an unexpected first impression, while playful artwork brings a sense of humour to the breakfast nook.Family history finds its way into the design, too. A vintage Elvis Presley lamp in the media room celebrates Hale’s Memphis roots and her grandmother’s affection for the musician. Custom stained-glass windows by Los Angeles artist Ben Tuna, known professionally as the Glass Cowboy, draw inspiration from her grandparents’ front door in Tennessee.These details make the interiors feel collected over time, with personal associations taking precedence over perfectly coordinated rooms.Spaces for reflection and remembranceBeyond its colourful finishes, the home’s most significant changes are deeply personal. Hale transformed a guest bedroom overlooking the canyon into a mint-green office where she works through scripts. A dedicated meditation room holds an altar to departed loved ones, alongside feathers and vintage Happy Meal toys.Photographs of family members line the hallway, while a white chair in the living room serves as a quiet reminder of her late father. These intimate touches give the home an emotional resonance that no design trend could replicate.The property remains a retreat from the outside world, but it is no longer simply a place to escape. Through three years of considered changes, Hale has created an environment that reflects her memories, her recovery and her growing sense of self. More than a renovation, the home is a portrait of a woman learning to make space for who she is today and who she hopes to become.Images Courtesy: Instagram/lucehalyYou use AI every day. articles.title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment
articles.summary: The doctor says she faced a brutal investigation after she passed on complaints brought to her by other doctors.
articles.body:
A doctor who raised concerns about the treatment of children questioning their gender has told the BBC she was accused of transphobia, bullied and harassed out of her child protection job in the NHS.

Dr Sarah Redvers, who was a named safeguarding GP, said she faced a brutal investigation after she passed on complaints brought to her by other doctors.

Speaking publicly for the first time, Redvers said she felt she was "silenced" for doing her job after questioning whether another GP was appropriately assessing the needs of young people who were distressed about their gender identity.

She has brought a claim of constructive dismissal against the NHS Sussex Integrated Care Board (ICB), which managed health services in the county, and Adam Doyle, who was the ICB's chief executive until 2025.

Redvers told a three-week employment tribunal hearing that she felt the focus on investigating her meant issues of patient safety had been sidelined.

Dozens of children put at risk after gender care failures at GP clinic, inquiry finds

Unacceptable waits for adult gender clinic appointments, review says

"I was just bewildered really that the medical and safeguarding issues were completely lost," she said. "It's really risky," she told the BBC.

NHS Surrey and Sussex said: "We recognise that some employment processes should have been handled differently." They have apologised to Redvers.

In June 2026, nearly six years after she first raised concerns, a separate NHS safety investigation found that dozens of children, some as young as 13, had been inappropriately prescribed drugs at the WellBN practice , the clinic where the other doctor worked.

The report said 78 children had potentially been harmed after puberty-blocking drugs and cross sex hormones were prescribed to them without proper checks.

The report said it was in response to a drug review carried out in autumn 2024, not to the concerns first raised by Redvers years earlier.

NHS England said: "It is totally unacceptable young people were put at risk of harm because some practitioners at the WellBN practice provided care they were not commissioned to deliver by the NHS."

"To read about a medical scandal knowing it could have been stopped was upsetting," said Redvers, "because concerns were raised appropriately and leaders knew about it".

Redvers, who has many years of experience working with vulnerable groups, was a named safeguarding GP for Sussex, which meant other doctors who had safety concerns about patients could turn to her for advice and help.

The tribunal heard that in July 2020, a doctor got in touch because she was worried about a patient who had gone to an online clinic which was registered overseas.

It wanted the GP to take over prescribing testosterone to a vulnerable 18-year-old female, who was distressed about her gender.

The doctor was also given advice on such prescriptions by a Brighton GP, Dr Sam Hall.

"The concerns to me were that Hall was recommending treatment for patients that he hadn't assessed, that he hadn't met, and that other GPs were uncomfortable with prescribing," Redvers said.

Redvers spoke to NHS England (NHSE) and was advised to make the complaint as a whistleblower.

It was investigated and NHSE said it was satisfied with Hall's practice.

Over the following months several other GPs voiced their concerns to Redvers about the quality of assessments, the prescription of puberty blocking drugs and cross sex hormones, and the lack of specialist supervision at the WellBN clinic, where Hall was based.

Again, the NHS investigated her concerns. She said she was also told by the investigator that there was a "general worry" that there "would be allegations of transphobia."

Hall, who is a trans man and was born female, qualified as a GP in 2019 and is known as a campaigner for transgender rights in Brighton.

Publicly, he had said that his own pain had shown him the importance of "affirmative care" - support for a patient in a way which accepts rather than challenges their preferred gender and treatment decisions follow from that.

He was also working with the NHS locally on setting up a Trans Health hub and with a Brighton trans support charity called The Clare Project.

The second NHS investigation considered "the full scope" of Hall's work and concluded there was no cause for concern. It also said there was "one colleague whose persistent interest in the issue appeared disproportionate." Redvers took that to mean her.

The concerns she said she and others were raising were about the quality of care being provided, and whether it had the necessary medical evidence to underpin it, not her views on gender.

"It's about medical assessment and treatment of patients, which is something we have to get right, particularly in this complex group of vulnerable patients," she said.

She said she viewed any suggestion of transphobia as "appalling," and it was "dangerous" that such claims were obscuring the medical and safeguarding issues she was raising.

In 2021, whilst waiting for the outcome of the second investigation and prompted by a concern raised by local mental health services about the care of a vulnerable 15-year-old, Redvers referred Hall to the medical regulator, the GMC.

Hall emailed Adam Doyle, then CEO of NHS Sussex, directly to complain.

"I am being victimised here, and I need proper protection from this individual and their repeated attempts to disrupt my career" he said.

Although Doyle at first denied to the tribunal he knew Hall before this, it emerged during the tribunal that he had previously had a number of mentoring meetings with the GP.

The GMC investigation was not taken forward. However, the NHS launched an investigation into Redvers, bringing in an external investigator.

The tribunal heard she was called to what she described as a "brutal" four-hour interrogation.

"It was oppressive, very upsetting. I didn't feel I had the chance at all to explain what had happened," she said. "I broke down at one point".

She said she was off sick for several months as a result and received treatment for trauma.

Other colleagues who were interviewed as part of the investigation into Redvers also complained about the process and the NHS upheld most of their complaints.

The investigation concluded the CEO and trust should apologise to Redvers.

It also warned that Redvers' treatment would have a "broader negative impact" on the willingness of staff to raise concerns.

In 2023, a year after the grievance outcome, when a trans campaigner suggested in an NHS meeting that she was transphobic, Redvers told the tribunal she felt the NHS did not do enough to support her. She felt she had no choice but to leave her job as a safeguarding GP.

"I just felt there's no way I could carry on working in this organisation," she told the BBC.

At about that time, a group of parents, school governors and social workers began raising concerns about WellBn and Hall.

The co-founder of campaign group PSHE Brighton, Rachel Cashman, said: "It is a travesty that Sarah Redvers was punished for doing her job safeguarding and expecting the best standards of care for gender distressed children."

Redvers is now waiting for the outcome of her employment tribunal. She may not get the judgment for several months.

She described what has happened as "personally and professionally difficult" and said the NHS "needs to remember that patients come first" and it should "listen to staff who raise legitimate concerns."

In a statement NHS Surrey and Sussex said: "We engaged professionally and supportively with the Employment Tribunal. We recognise that some employment processes should have been handled differently and have apologised whilst Dr Redvers was employed with us, before, and during the hearings. We await the findings of the tribunal to make any further comment."

NHS England said: "When concerns about prescribing practices by an individual GP were escalated to NHS England national directors in 2023, they met directly with an affected family and asked regional professional standards leads to undertake formal investigations.

"Wider concerns were subsequently identified, and the WellBN practice was asked to stop providing a specialised prescribing service. Further new information led to NHS England and NHS Sussex initiating an independent patient safety investigation in 2025."

Dr Sam Hall and WellBN have been contacted for comment.

In response to the investigation report in June, WellBN said it recognised "the seriousness and sensitivity of the matters raised" and that its priority remained providing "compassionate, safe and effective care for all patients".

articles.title: In 2005, Montana ranchers bought land unaware fossils lay beneath it; a nearly complete T. rex found there later sold to a Dutch museum for millions
articles.summary: In 2005, ranchers Mary Ann and Lige Murray purchased land in Montana, unknowingly acquiring dinosaur fossils that would lead to millions in sales and a legal dispute about ownership of the fossils. The Montana Supreme Court ultimately ruled on the ownership of these prehistoric treasures, determining the uniqueness of fossils versus traditional mineral rights.
articles.body: In 2005, Mary Ann and Lige Murray bought the entire surface estate of a ranch near Jordan, Montana, without knowing that dinosaur fossils lay beneath it. According to the Montana Supreme Court’s 2020 opinion, the sale divided ownership, with the Murrays receiving the surface rights and one-third of the mineral rights. The previous owners, Jerry and Robert Severson, retained the remaining two-thirds of the mineral interestsOther discoveries included a nearly complete Tyrannosaurus rex, which, per the court’s opinion, the Murrays sold to a Dutch museum in 2014 for several million dollars. The proceeds were held in escrow against the backdrop of both sides disputing ownership. Ultimately, the case reached the state’s highest court, which ruled on 20 May 2020 that the dinosaur fossils within the scope of a deed’s general mineral reservation were not categorised as minerals unless the deed itself explicitly said otherwise.Fossils turn a land sale into an ownership disputeAutumn 2005 was the year when the Murrays’ discoveries started, after they had found a cluster of fossilised spikes on the ranch. Just a year later, in 2006, amateur palaeontologist Clayton Phipps discovered the specimens which later came to be known as the “Duelling Dinosaurs”. These two specimens included a carnivorous theropod, which was about 22 feet (7 metres), and the other one was a 28-foot (9 metres) herbivorous ceratopsian. According to Phys Org’s report, they had been found with imprints of their skin and died around 66 million years ago in combat.This would not be the end of discoveries; in 2007, a Triceratops foot was found, and later in 2011, a Triceratops skull turned up. In the market, the Triceratops foot was sold for $20,000, while the skull was offered between $200,000 and $250,000; in the case of the “Duelling Dinosaurs”, their value was estimated at several million dollars because of their rarity and scientific importance.Although the Murrays were potentially on the way to riches, they couldn’t immediately cash in on their discoveries because potential buyers wanted to know whether they had the rights to sell the “Duelling Dinosaurs”. To their dismay, the situation only escalated in 2013, when the Seversons claimed ownership over the specimens through their mineral rights. In response to the situation, the Murrays sought a court declaration that they were entitled to the discoveries since they held ownership of the surface estate.Montana court defines the scope of mineral rightsA federal district court ruled for the Murrays in 2016 and found that fossils fell outside the definition of what minerals really mean. Their value, the court reasoned, depended on completeness, species, and preservation, rather than simply on mineral composition. Fossils are neither mined, processed, nor smelted, the Murrays’ attorney argued, setting them apart from the oil, coal, or gold that mineral rights have traditionally covered in Montana. Subsequently, the Ninth Circuit asked the Montana high court to resolve the issue under state law, and in evaluating the case, the court scrutinised the specific wording and context of the deed.The bottom line of the ruling favoured the Murrays, as the court reasoned fossils are prized because they are remnants of prehistoric creatures. Their value isn’t found in mineral content, which makes them viable as raw material for manufacturing fuel, goods, or jewellery. Furthermore, fossils are often brought to the surface by soil erosion, and their excavation interferes with the land above; these features are what separate them from resources that fall under mineral rights. In 2019, Montana’s law placed dinosaur fossils in the surface estate unless a transaction document specified otherwise, but excluded cases already before the courts.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trains cancelled and roads warnings as Scotland prepares for Storm Boelo
articles.summary: Heavy rain and strong winds are expected during the second named storm to hit in two days, with gusts of up to 80mph forecast.
articles.body:
Train services have been cancelled and police have warned against unnecessary road journeys as Scotland prepares for the arrival of Storm Boelo.

Heavy rain and strong winds are expected during the second named storm to hit in two days, with gusts of up to 80mph forecast.

Most of the country is covered by a yellow Met Office warning from midday on Saturday, while a more severe amber alert takes effect from 21:00 on Saturday until 21:00 on Sunday, covering the mainland and Western Isles.

Forecasters say the storm, which is the second named storm in two days, could result in injury, flying debris, power cuts and damage to trees and buildings.

Scotland to be hit with 80mph wind gusts as Storm Boelo alert upgraded to amber

Major travel disruption and thousands without power as Storm Austen hits UK

Although the 24-hour amber warning is not unprecedented, it is unusual because of the length of time it will be in place over such a wide geographical area.

On Friday the forecast triggered a meeting of the Scottish government's resilience room which ensures the country is prepared for severe weather events.

Storm Boelo will bring very strong westerly winds with widespread gusts of 60-70mph (96.6-112.7km/h), and gusts up to 80mph (128.7km/h) in exposed coastal areas.

The strongest winds will initially affect western Scotland and the far north of Northern Ireland on Saturday evening and then spread eastwards overnight and through Sunday.

This will be accompanied by periods of heavy rain and frequent showers.

Forecasters warned that flying debris could cause injuries and danger to life, with a good chance of power cuts and an impact on phone coverage.

The Met Office also warned of damage to trees and buildings, bridge closures and transport disruption.

Winds will gradually ease from the west through Sunday.

Public transport is still running, though ScotRail has confirmed that some train services will be cancelled:

Glasgow Central – Ayr line will close between Kilwinning and Ayr from 21:00 on Saturday

Glasgow Queen Street – Oban / Mallaig line will close between Fort William and Mallaig and between Crianlarich and Oban from around 22:00

Inverness – Kyle of Lochalsh line will close between Kyle of Lochalsh and Achnashellach from the start of service on Sunday

Inverness – Wick / Thurso line will close between Helmsdale and Wick / Thurso from the start of service on Sunday

Network Rail said trains will also run at reduced speeds across large parts of Scotland from Saturday night into Sunday.

Passengers are advised to expect significant disruption and longer journeys, and are should check services before they travel.

Supt Andy Barclay, deputy head of road policing for Police Scotland, warned drivers that conditions may be hazardous and urged them to consider whether journeys were "really necessary" over the weekend.

Stopping distances can be at least double on wet roads compared to dry conditions, and spray can reduce driver visibility

HGV and bus drivers should drive with extreme caution and be aware you may be asked to park at a suitable position by the police

If you need to travel, please drive to the conditions and allow extra time for your journey

Stay tuned to media outlets for further updates and consult the Traffic Scotland website and social media channels for information relating to affected roads

As for coastal areas, the Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) said that weather conditions pose a safety risk to visitors and advised "extreme caution" if people are near the shoreline, especially along exposed cliffs, seafronts and piers.

The charity's water safety lead, Michael Avril, urged people to keep a safe distance from the water as conditions "could knock you off your feet or wash you into the sea".

CalMac cancelled a number of sailings on Friday and has amended the Saturday timetable for MV Isle of Mull - which runs between the mainland, South Uist and Barra.

It may be that some events are postponed during stormy conditions. Friday's Scottish Cup tie between Penicuik Athletic and Clyde was among the first to be delayed because of heavy rain.

Western Isles Council said events including church services should be aware of strong winds throughout Sunday and advised they "plan accordingly".

Paisley's popular Halloween festival is due to take place this weekend, which includes a parade, street theatre and outdoor light installations.

Renfrewshire Council said Friday's programme would go ahead as planned, but that an update on Saturday's events would be provided closer to the time.

And a Halloween family fun day at Dean Park Castle and Country Park in Kilmarnock, scheduled for Sunday, has been postponed due to the weather warning.

articles.title: Your pillows may be past their prime — here’s how often experts say you should replace them
articles.summary: Experts share how often you should clean pillows and when it’s time to replace them. Plus, how to keep pillows in great shape over time.
articles.body: Bed pillows go through a lot of wear and tear over the years, particularly if you move around a lot in your sleep. Plus, pillows have direct contact with all of the oils and skin care products on your face, which means they need to be washed often. But how often should you actually clean your pillows and when do you know it’s time to just throw them away and invest in a new set? I spoke with cleaning experts to learn more about how often you should clean and replace your pillows and what signs you should look for to determine when to do one or the other. Plus, I asked experts the best way to clean pillows (not just pillowcases) depending on what type they are. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. How often should you clean and replace your pillows? “I recommend cleaning pillows every three to six months and while there’s no hard expiration date, I generally expect to replace pillows every year or two,” says Robin Murphy, a cleaning expert and chief cleaning officer at home cleaning company Maid Brigade. “What matters is their condition. If your pillow is lumpy, stays flat after fluffing, has a persistent odor, or no longer supports your head and neck comfortably, it’s probably time for a new one.” The best products for cleaning and replacing pillows All of the products below have at least a four-star average from 500 or more shoppers on Amazon. Some of the recommendations below are also based on guidance from experts. You can add these balls to the dryer after washing your down alternative pillows. Made entirely from wool from New Zealand sheep, the dryer balls help pillows dry fast and soften fabrics, according to the brand. Plus, they also help reduce static and wrinkles in clothing. These should help maintain the filling of pillows and prevent it from clumping. This is technically a laundry sanitizer, not a detergent, so it’s meant to be used with detergent, and its main job is to get rid of bacteria and odors. The bleach-free sanitizer is safe to use on multiple types of apparel and fabrics. Plus, it’s effective in cold water and suitable for clothing of all different shades. Additionally, people who bought it say that it does a great job of getting rid of odors, and that one shopper even notes that it’s effective on pillows. You can pair this with Tide’s Free & Clear laundry detergent, which is my go-to mild detergent when I’m washing something delicate that I don’t want ruined in the washing machine. If you want to clean a pillow that doesn’t smell great without having to actually put it in the washer, you should also try this fabric refresher spray from Febreeze. It’s great for freshening up clothing or fabrics that aren’t machine washable or ones that are very sensitive to machine washing. Plus, the brand even mentions that it’s suitable for deodorizing things like pillows and sofas. Shoppers agree, confirming that they use it on things like pillows and furniture. Both experts I spoke to recommend keeping a pillow protector on your pillow in addition to a pillow case. Pillow protectors are to your pillows what mattress protectors are to your mattress — they keep out water and bed bugs. These are hypoallergenic, according to the brand, so they’re also great if you have sensitive skin. They’re available in terry cloth and cotton. Plus, the protectors are available in sizes for king and queen pillows, as well as for travel-size and body pillows. Purple’s ultra-popular Harmony pillow is a latex pillow with a honeycomb gel wrap that eases several pressure points to offer better sleep, according to the brand. It’s available in multiple lofts (thickness), and in both standard and king sizes. The brand recommends the 5.5-inch loft for stomach and back sleepers and 6.5-inch and 7.5-inch pillows for side sleepers. If you’re ready to start fresh with a new set of clean pillows, this is a highly-reviewed option that shoppers say is also breathable. How do you clean a pillow? How you clean a pillow depends on what type it is, particularly if the filling is made from memory foam versus a down alternative and polyester. Kadi Dulude, a cleaning expert and the owner of home cleaning company Wizard of Homes, recommends paying attention to what the care label says on your pillow before laundering it, but in general you should wash machine-washable pillows two to four times a year. “Memory foam pillows can’t be machine washed but they have a tight cover on them that you can wash instead,” she says. Murphy also recommends using a gentle cycle with mild detergent to wash pillows. “Wash two at a time to balance the machine, and dry thoroughly on low heat with dryer balls to prevent clumping.” For memory foam pillows, Murphy recommends spot-cleaning the actual pillow and, like Dulude mentioned above, only washing the cover. Both Dulude and Murphy recommend using pillow protectors in addition to pillowcases to help prolong the quality of your pillows. How to clean a machine-washable pillow: Remove the pillowcase from your pillow and place the pillow in your washing machine drum. Murphy recommends washing two at once since it will help balance out the weight around the machine’s agitators. Start a gentle cycle and only use mild detergent; wash the pillows the same as your regular clothing. To dry, Murphy recommends putting the pillows in a dryer and using low heat and dryer balls, which will help prevent the filling from clumping. Allow them to dry completely before putting any covers back on them to prevent mildew from growing on them, says Murphy. How to clean memory foam and latex pillows: Since memory foam and latex pillow are often not machine washable, both Dulude and Murphy recommend removing the cover from them (not just the pillowcase) and washing the cover. To clean the actual pillow, Murphy recommends spot cleaning, which includes using products like gentle fabric sprays or stain removers to get rid of stains and odors, as opposed to drenching the entire pillow in water. Allow them to dry completely before putting the cover and pillow case back on. How do you know when it’s time to replace your pillows? The best way to tell when it’s time to get a new set of pillows has everything to do with their appearance and feel. “[Replace your pillow] when you see it’s lost its shape, is lumpy and is not giving the support it used to,” says Dulude. “And of course when you can see discoloration/stains that can’t be washed out.” Meet our cleaning experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Kadi Dulude is a cleaning expert and the owner of home cleaning company Wizard of Homes. Robin Murphy is a cleaning expert, chief cleaning officer at home cleaning services company Maid Brigade and writer at cleaning site Who Likes It Dirty. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected, where I write about home and kitchen appliances, cleaning and more.
